newsitem.title: POLAND: Isuzu to invest DM 380 mln in Polish plant.
newsitem.headline: Isuzu to invest DM 380 mln in Polish plant.

text.p: Japan's Isuzu Motors Ltd plans to invest 380 million marks ($245.7 million) in Poland to produce diesel engines and export them to European Union countries, the Polish industry minister said on Tuesday.
"The construction of the Isuzu diesel engine factory is likely to start in April next year and be completed in June 1999," Klemens Scierski told a news briefing.
"The engines will be state-of-the-art... and will mostly be exported to the European Union," he said.
He said the factory would employ 400 workers and have an annual output of 300,000 engines and annual sales of about one billion marks.
The engines will be designed for Opel passenger cars, producted by General Motors' German subsidiary Adam Opel AG. General Motors hold a 37.4-percent stake in Isuzu.

The engine plant will most likely be located in the southern city of Tychy, in an economic zone in the industrial region of Silesia, where investors are offered a break on Poland's 40 percent corporate tax for 10 years.
Earlier this year Adam Opel launched the construction of a car assembly factory in the same zone. The plant will assemble about 72,000 cars from 1998.
